pins.title: A gift for new hikers
items: What To Do If You Get Lost
pins.sub: 7 printable guides, $29.99. Instant PDF, nothing to ship.

pins.title: Bring a page to stamp
pins.sub: Most visitor centers keep a free ink stamp with the park's name and date. Stamp it and log the trail beside it.

pins.title: Leave the jeans home
pins.sub: Wet cotton stays cold and heavy for hours. Quick-dry nylon with some stretch dries while you walk.

pins.title: Water-resistant is not waterproof
pins.sub: Water-resistant handles a light drizzle. Waterproof means taped seams and a membrane. Open the vents when you climb.

pins.title: The 5-second pole check
pins.sub: Set the length, close every lock all the way, then press your full weight into the pole on flat ground. If it moves, tighten it.

pins.kicker: Even on a short fall hike
pins.title: Pack the Ten Essentials
pins.sub: Navigation, a headlamp, sun protection, first aid, a knife, fire starter, shelter, plus extra food, water and clothes.

pins.title: Get there early
pins.sub: While the shuttle runs, the canyon road is closed to cars and the visitor center lot fills early on busy days. Check nps.gov for this season's schedule.

pins.title: 5 classic hikes
pins.sub: Round-trip distances from the NPS. A parking tag is needed to park over 15 minutes.

pins.title: Pick the right trail
pins.sub: 2 to 5 miles round trip, under 1,000 ft of climbing, and a clear payoff like a waterfall, lake or viewpoint.
